data.description:
## Problem

On 2026-09-10 the `tickets` branch gained 28,570 previously-unreachable commits in a single reconciler sync, moving a fresh blobless tickets-only pack from 496,938 KiB to 598,124 KiB in roughly 30 minutes. Baseline growth either side of the event is ~2.5 to ~3.9 MiB/day, so this was about 40 days of ordinary growth arriving at once.

## Evidence

Measured during the investigation on `stable-jobless-coot`:

```
0e2a06ba03f5e32d25a8dac036be938177ade9a3
  parents=92f8d2783e41c137d58ac91aff5ba46f6845a5c4
  date=2026-09-10 18:28:21 +0000
  subject=ticket: LINK 40d7-eca8-8726-4b14

924a93f21edf6c4066339feeb7fff2294244d917
  parents=540983c7e841f9c739c286d0292a3e28d7312f30
  date=2026-09-10 18:43:18 +0000
  subject=chore: sync events from rebar reconciler [run 34514936676]

is_below_ancestor_of_above=no
is_above_ancestor_of_tip=yes

unique commits introduced = 28570
oldest_new = b46a31cacd45c3d34ea8697a5eb47462f394599a  2026-08-29 18:49:43 +0000  ticket: EDIT 9d40-1db8-1bcc-4f91
newest_new = 924a93f21edf6c4066339feeb7fff2294244d917  2026-09-10 18:43:18 +0000
```

The later commit is not a descendant of the earlier one. A side history reaching back to 2026-08-29 became reachable from the branch tip in one step.

## Why this needs its own investigation

The two candidate readings have opposite implications and the Git evidence alone does not separate them:

- **Recovery.** The reconciler reattached genuinely valid ticket history that had become unreachable, in which case the branch was previously missing events and the real defect is whatever detached them.
- **Duplication.** The reconciler grafted a parallel line of already-represented events onto the tip, in which case the store now carries a duplicate history and will accumulate more on the next occurrence.

Under the first reading the event was a repair. Under the second it was corruption that a repair-shaped commit message conceals. Both produce the same reachability jump, so the distinction has to come from the reconciler's code path and its run log, not from the graph.

A merge commit observed nearby on 2026-09-09, `Merge origin/tickets (auto-reconcile during push retry)`, suggests the auto-reconcile-on-push-retry path as the place to start. That is a starting point, not a conclusion.

## Relationship to other work

This is the mechanism behind the step change that pushed the authorship gate's pack budget over its limit (`stable-jobless-coot`). Fixing that gate addresses where the measurement is taken; it does not address a reconciler that can add tens of thousands of commits in one sync. If the duplication reading is correct, ADR 0106's history reclamation work would also be reclaiming against a store that keeps re-growing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reconciler run `34514936676` is inspected and the code path that produced commit `924a93f21edf6c4066339feeb7fff2294244d917` is identified in source.
- [ ] The event is classified as recovery or duplication on evidence — specifically, whether the 28,570 commits carry events already represented on the branch before the sync.
- [ ] If duplication: the conditions that trigger it are reproduced in a test, and the reconciler no longer grafts a parallel history under those conditions.
- [ ] If recovery: the defect that made valid ticket history unreachable is identified and tracked, since silent event loss is the more serious of the two findings.
- [ ] Whether the condition has recurred since 2026-09-10 is established by measurement rather than assumed from the absence of reports.
data.title: Reconciler sync made 28,570 older commits reachable on tickets in one step: recovery or duplicated history is unestablished
